title: Identify Functions
student_objective: I can decide whether a relation shown verbally, in a table, on a graph, with ordered pairs, in a mapping, or symbolically defines a function.
teacher_objective: Diagnose confusion between repeated inputs and repeated outputs, misuse of the vertical line test, and symbolic relations that give one input more than one output.

concept_cards.title: Function rule
concept_cards.content: A relation is a function when every input is paired with exactly one output.

concept_cards.title: Repeated outputs are allowed
concept_cards.content: Different inputs may share the same output. That does not break the function rule.

concept_cards.title: Repeated inputs can be a problem
concept_cards.content: If the same input is paired with two different outputs, the relation is not a function.

concept_cards.title: Tables and ordered pairs
concept_cards.content: Check the x-values or first coordinates. If one input has two different outputs, the relation is not a function.

concept_cards.title: Graphs: vertical line test
concept_cards.content: A graph represents y as a function of x when every vertical line hits the graph at most once.

concept_cards.title: Equations and rules
concept_cards.content: Ask whether each x-value determines exactly one y-value. For example, y=2x+3 is a function, while x=y² is not because one x can give two y-values.

items.prompt: Does the relation {(1,4),(2,5),(3,6)} define a function? Answer function or not a function.
hint_steps: Look only at the first coordinate in each ordered pair.
Ask whether any input is paired with two different outputs.
The inputs 1, 2, and 3 each have exactly one output, so the answer is function.

solution_steps.explanation: List the first coordinates.
No input is paired with two different outputs.
Every input has exactly one output.

alternate_solution_steps.explanation: Trace one output from each input.
That is exactly the definition of a function.

teaching_explanation.title: Use the input test
teaching_explanation.overview: A function assigns exactly one output to each input.
teaching_explanation.vocabulary: Input = x-value or first coordinate. Output = y-value or second coordinate.

items.prompt: Does the relation {(2,1),(2,5),(4,7)} define a function? Answer function or not a function.
hint_steps: Find repeated first coordinates.
The input 2 is paired with both 1 and 5.
One input has two different outputs, so the answer is not a function.

solution_steps.explanation: The same input has two outputs.
That violates the definition of a function.
A function cannot assign two outputs to one input.

teaching_explanation.title: Find the repeated input
teaching_explanation.overview: One repeated input with different outputs is enough to make the relation not a function.
teaching_explanation.vocabulary: Repeated outputs are allowed; repeated inputs with different outputs are not.

items.prompt: A table has x-values 0,1,2,3 and y-values 5,5,7,7. Does the table define a function?
hint_steps: Check the inputs, not the outputs.
Different inputs are allowed to share the same output.
Every x-value has exactly one y-value, so the answer is function.

solution_steps.explanation: Read each row as one input-output pair.
Repeated outputs are allowed.
Every input has exactly one output.

teaching_explanation.title: Repeated outputs are okay
teaching_explanation.overview: A function may send several different inputs to the same output.
teaching_explanation.vocabulary: The restriction is on inputs, not on outputs.

items.prompt: A mapping shows -2→4, 0→4, and 3→9. Is the relation a function?

solution_steps.explanation: Trace the arrows from the inputs.
No input points to two outputs.
Sharing output 4 is allowed.

items.prompt: A mapping shows 1→3 and 1→6, while 2→8. Is the relation a function?

solution_steps.explanation: Input 1 has two arrows.
That fails the function rule.
Every input must have exactly one output.

items.prompt: Does the equation y=2x-5 define y as a function of x?

solution_steps.explanation: For any chosen x, the rule calculates one value of y.
There is no second output choice.
Each input determines exactly one output.

items.prompt: Does the equation x=y² define y as a function of x over the real numbers?

solution_steps.explanation: Test whether one x-value can give more than one y-value.
One input has two outputs.
The relation fails the function rule.

items.prompt: Does {(0,2),(1,2),(2,2)} define a function?
hint_steps: Circle the x-values.
Repeated y-values are allowed.
0, 1, and 2 each have exactly one output, so the answer is function.

solution_steps.explanation: The first coordinates are all different.
Repeated outputs do not break a function.
Each input has exactly one output.

items.prompt: The table has rows (-1,3), (0,4), (1,5), and (1,8). Is it a function?
hint_steps: Scan the x-column for repeats.
A repeated x-value matters when it has different y-values.
x=1 has outputs 5 and 8, so the answer is not a function.

solution_steps.explanation: The same input has two outputs.
That violates the definition.
The table does not define a function.

items.prompt: A graph consists of the points (-2,1), (0,3), (2,1), and (4,3). Does it define a function?
hint_steps: Imagine a vertical line through each plotted x-value.
Check whether two points are stacked above the same x-value.
No two points share an x-coordinate, so the graph passes the vertical line test and is a function.

solution_steps.explanation: Each plotted point has a different x-coordinate.

solution_steps.equation: vertical line hits at most once
solution_steps.explanation: No x-value has two y-values.
The graph passes the vertical line test.

items.prompt: Does {(5,1),(6,1),(7,2),(8,2)} define a function?
hint_steps: Check the first coordinates.
Repeated outputs are allowed.
Every input has exactly one output, so the answer is function.

solution_steps.explanation: Each input has one output.
The relation meets the function rule.

items.prompt: A table has x-values -2,-1,0,0 and y-values 3,4,5,6. Is it a function?
hint_steps: Look for a repeated x-value.
The input 0 has two different y-values.
Because x=0 has outputs 5 and 6, the answer is not a function.

solution_steps.explanation: One input has two outputs.
That violates the definition.

items.prompt: A vertical line at x=2 intersects a graph at y=-1 and y=4. Does the graph define y as a function of x?
hint_steps: Use the vertical line test.
The same vertical line hits the graph twice.
One x-value has two y-values, so the graph is not a function.

solution_steps.explanation: The same input has two outputs.
The graph fails the vertical line test.

items.prompt: Does y=x²+1 define y as a function of x?
hint_steps: Choose any x-value and evaluate x²+1.
Each x produces one numerical result.
Each input has one output, so the relation is a function.

solution_steps.explanation: The rule produces one y-value for each x-value.
Each input determines exactly one output.

items.prompt: Does x²+y²=25 define y as a function of x over the real numbers?
hint_steps: Try x=0.
When x=0, y²=25, so y can be 5 or -5.
One input gives two outputs, so the relation is not a function.

solution_steps.explanation: Test one convenient input.
The same input has two outputs.
One counterexample is enough.

items.prompt: Does {(1,9),(2,9),(3,10),(4,10)} define a function?

solution_steps.explanation: No input repeats with a different output.
Repeated outputs are allowed.

items.prompt: A graph has points (0,1), (0,-1), and (2,3). Does it define a function?

solution_steps.explanation: Two points share the same x-value.
A vertical line at x=0 hits twice.

items.prompt: Does y=-3x+7 define y as a function of x?

solution_steps.explanation: Each x-value produces one y-value.
The function rule is satisfied.

items.prompt: Does x=y²+1 define y as a function of x over the real numbers?

solution_steps.explanation: Choose an input that creates two possible y-values.
One input has two outputs.
The relation fails the function rule.

items.prompt: A table repeats the output 6 for three different input values, but no input repeats. Does it define a function?
items.explanation_prompt: Why is this still a function even though the output 6 repeats?
items.explanation_guidance: Explain the rule using inputs and outputs.

solution_steps.explanation: Sharing an output is allowed.
No input has two different outputs.
The relation satisfies the definition.

practice_bank.hint: Check whether any first coordinate has two outputs.

solution_steps.explanation: Every input has one output.

practice_bank.hint: The repeated pair gives the same output, not a different output.

solution_steps.explanation: Duplicating the same pair does not create a second output.

practice_bank.prompt: A graph passes the vertical line test. Does it define y as a function of x?
practice_bank.hint: Passing the vertical line test means each x has at most one y.

solution_steps.equation: every vertical line hits at most once
solution_steps.explanation: That is the graph test for a function.

practice_bank.prompt: A graph fails the vertical line test. Does it define y as a function of x?
practice_bank.hint: A vertical line hitting twice means one x has two y-values.

solution_steps.equation: one vertical line hits more than once
solution_steps.explanation: One input has multiple outputs.

practice_bank.prompt: Every book ISBN is paired with exactly one publication title. Is title a function of ISBN?
practice_bank.hint: Ask how many titles each ISBN is assigned.

solution_steps.explanation: Each input has exactly one output.
